dryer-not-heating.title: Dryer Not Heating? Here Is What Is Usually Wrong
dryer-not-heating.seo_title: Dryer Not Heating? Causes and Fixes
dryer-not-heating.meta_description: Dryer runs but no heat? The usual causes are a blown thermal fuse, a failed element or igniter, or a blocked vent. What to check and when to call.
dryer-not-heating.excerpt: A dryer that tumbles without heating almost always comes down to one of five parts, or to a vent that can no longer move air. Here is how to tell them apart.

faqs.q: Why does my dryer run but not heat?
faqs.a: The drum motor and the heating circuit are separate, so the dryer can tumble normally while the heat is dead. On electric models the usual causes are a blown thermal fuse, a broken heating element or a failed thermostat; on gas models it is the igniter or the gas valve coils. A blocked vent is the most common underlying cause of all of them.

faqs.q: Can a blocked vent stop a dryer from heating?
faqs.a: Yes. When lint blocks the duct, hot moist air cannot escape, the dryer overheats and the safety devices cut the heat — often by blowing the thermal fuse permanently. This is the most common cause we find, and clearing the vent is part of the repair.

faqs.q: Is it worth repairing a dryer that will not heat?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Thermal fuses, elements, igniters, coils and thermostats are inexpensive, contained parts, and the repair is normally completed in a single visit. The free estimate lets you compare the cost against a new dryer before deciding.

faqs.q: My electric dryer tumbles but has no heat. Could it be the breaker?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is worth checking first. An electric dryer runs on a double 240-volt breaker. If one leg trips, the drum still turns on 120 volts while the element gets no power. Switch the breaker fully off and back on before booking a visit.

faqs.q: How long does a dryer heating repair take?
faqs.a: Most are finished in the same visit. The technician tests the heating circuit, replaces the failed part and checks vent airflow before leaving, and the work is covered by our 90-day warranty on parts and labor.

dishwasher-not-draining.title: Dishwasher Not Draining? Causes and What To Check
dishwasher-not-draining.seo_title: Dishwasher Not Draining: Causes and Fixes
dishwasher-not-draining.meta_description: Water left in the bottom of the dishwasher? The usual causes are a clogged filter, a blocked drain hose, a jammed pump or a plugged air gap. What to check.
dishwasher-not-draining.excerpt: Standing water at the end of a cycle means the drain path is blocked somewhere between the filter and the sink. Here is how to find out where.

faqs.q: Why is there water in the bottom of my dishwasher?
faqs.a: Because the drain path is blocked or the drain pump is not running. The most frequent causes are a clogged filter, debris jamming the pump, a kinked or greasy drain hose, a blocked air gap at the sink, or a garbage disposal knockout plug that was never removed.

faqs.q: Can I fix a dishwasher that will not drain myself?
faqs.a: Some of it, safely. Switch the machine off at the breaker, remove and rinse the filter, clear the sump, clean the air gap and straighten the drain hose. If it still holds water after that, the pump or the control is involved and needs a technician.

faqs.q: Should I pour drain cleaner into the dishwasher?
faqs.a: No. Drain cleaner does not reach the blockage, and it damages the seals, hoses and plastic components inside the machine. Clearing the filter, hose and air gap mechanically is the correct approach.

faqs.q: My dishwasher stopped draining right after a new garbage disposal was installed. Why?
faqs.a: New disposals ship with a knockout plug blocking the dishwasher inlet, and it has to be removed during installation. If it was missed, the dishwasher has nowhere to drain. It is a quick fix once identified.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to fix a dishwasher that will not drain?
faqs.a: It depends on whether the fault is a blockage or a failed part. The technician diagnoses it at your home and gives you a free estimate before any work starts, so you see the price before deciding.

ice-maker-not-making-ice.title: Ice Maker Not Making Ice? Here Is Why
ice-maker-not-making-ice.seo_title: Ice Maker Not Making Ice? Causes and Fixes
ice-maker-not-making-ice.meta_description: Ice maker stopped producing? Usually a frozen fill tube, a failed water inlet valve, a closed shut-off arm or a freezer that is too warm. What to check first.
ice-maker-not-making-ice.excerpt: An ice maker that has stopped producing usually has a water supply problem, a temperature problem or a worn module. Each one looks different once you know what to check.

faqs.q: Why did my ice maker suddenly stop making ice?
faqs.a: The most common reasons are a frozen fill tube, a failed water inlet valve, a shut-off arm knocked into the stop position, or a freezer that has drifted above about 5 °F. A clogged water filter and a worn ice maker module are the next most likely.

faqs.q: How cold does a freezer need to be to make ice?
faqs.a: Roughly 0 to 5 °F. Above that the harvest cycle slows down and eventually stops, so an ice maker that has quit is sometimes really a refrigerator problem — usually a dirty condenser, a failing evaporator fan or a defrost fault.

faqs.q: Can I thaw a frozen ice maker myself?
faqs.a: You can thaw a frozen fill tube carefully with a hair dryer on a low setting, held at a distance, after unplugging the refrigerator. Never chip at ice with a knife or screwdriver — puncturing the mold or a refrigerant line turns a small job into an expensive one.

faqs.q: Why is my ice maker producing small or hollow cubes?
faqs.a: That is a water flow problem rather than a dead ice maker: usually a clogged water filter, a partly closed supply valve or a failing inlet valve that does not fill the mold completely.

faqs.q: Is it worth repairing an ice maker?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Fill valves, filters, fill tubes and ice maker modules are contained, affordable parts, and the repair is typically done in one visit. You get a free estimate first so you can compare before deciding.

oven-not-heating.title: Oven Not Heating? Gas and Electric Causes Explained
oven-not-heating.seo_title: Oven Not Heating? Causes and What To Check
oven-not-heating.meta_description: Oven will not heat but the cooktop works? On gas ranges it is usually the igniter; on electric, the bake element or sensor. What to check and when to call.
oven-not-heating.excerpt: An oven that will not heat while the burners work normally points at the oven circuit alone — and on a gas range that almost always means the igniter.

faqs.q: Why does my gas oven not heat when the burners work?
faqs.a: The cooktop burners and the oven use separate ignition systems. The oven has its own igniter and gas safety valve, and as the igniter weakens it still glows but no longer draws enough current to open that valve. The burners keep working normally while the oven never lights.

faqs.q: How do I know if my oven igniter is bad?
faqs.a: Watch the oven through the window after setting a bake temperature. If the igniter glows orange for three to four minutes and no flame appears, the igniter is almost certainly the problem. The definitive test is measuring the current it draws, which a technician does with a meter.

faqs.q: Can I replace an oven heating element myself?
faqs.a: On an electric oven it is a simpler job than a gas repair, but the circuit carries 240 volts and the breaker must be off before you touch anything. If you are not confident testing continuity, a technician can confirm the element is actually the failed part before anything is replaced.

faqs.q: My oven heats but the temperature is wrong. Is that the same problem?
faqs.a: No, that is usually the oven temperature sensor drifting, or a control board that is no longer regulating correctly. We test actual cavity temperature with a thermometer rather than trusting the display.

faqs.q: Is it worth repairing an oven that will not heat?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Igniters, elements and sensors are affordable, contained parts and the repair is normally completed in one visit — far less than replacing a range, especially a built-in wall oven sized to your cabinetry.

freezer-not-freezing.title: Freezer Not Freezing? Causes and What To Check
freezer-not-freezing.seo_title: Freezer Not Freezing? Causes and Fixes
freezer-not-freezing.meta_description: Freezer running but not freezing? Usually a dirty condenser, a stopped evaporator fan, a defrost fault or a bad door seal. What to check before calling.
freezer-not-freezing.excerpt: A freezer that runs constantly but never gets cold enough usually has an airflow problem, not a dead compressor. Here is how to narrow it down.

faqs.q: What temperature should a freezer be?
faqs.a: Around 0 °F. Anything consistently above about 10 °F will let food deteriorate and usually means an airflow or defrost problem rather than a dead compressor.

faqs.q: Why is my freezer running constantly but not cold?
faqs.a: Almost always because heat is not leaving the cabinet or cold air is not circulating inside it. A condenser packed with dust, a stopped evaporator fan, an iced-over evaporator coil or a failed door gasket all produce exactly that symptom.

faqs.q: Why does ice keep building up on the back wall of my freezer?
faqs.a: That is the defrost system failing. The heater, the defrost thermostat or the control that runs them has stopped, so frost accumulates over the evaporator until airflow is blocked. A torn door gasket letting humid Houston air in accelerates it.

faqs.q: Can a garage freezer work in Houston summers?
faqs.a: It depends on the model. Many freezers specify a minimum and maximum ambient temperature, and a hot garage pushes them to the edge. Keeping the condenser clean makes a large difference, and some units are built specifically for garage use.

faqs.q: Is it worth repairing a freezer that will not freeze?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Fans, defrost heaters, thermostats and gaskets are affordable, contained parts. A sealed-system failure is the one case where replacement often makes more sense, and we tell you that plainly at the free estimate.

garbage-disposal-humming.title: Garbage Disposal Humming But Not Working?
garbage-disposal-humming.seo_title: Garbage Disposal Humming But Not Working?
garbage-disposal-humming.meta_description: Disposal hums but will not grind? The plate is jammed. Here is how to shut it off safely, what causes jams and when the motor needs replacing instead.
garbage-disposal-humming.excerpt: A humming disposal has power but a jammed grinding plate. Keep flipping the switch and you will burn out the motor — here is what to do instead.

faqs.q: Why does my garbage disposal hum but not grind?
faqs.a: The motor has power but the grinding plate is jammed, usually by a bone fragment, fruit pit, piece of glass or a utensil. Holding the switch on while it hums overheats a stalled motor, so switch it off and clear the jam instead.

faqs.q: How do I unjam a garbage disposal safely?
faqs.a: Switch it off at the wall first. Look into the chamber with a flashlight and remove anything visible with tongs, never your fingers. Then work the hex key into the socket on the underside of the unit and rock the plate back and forth until it turns freely, and press the red reset button before restoring power.

faqs.q: What is the red button on the bottom of my disposal?
faqs.a: It is the overload reset. When the motor draws too much current — usually because of a jam — the overload trips and cuts power to protect it. Pressing it restores power, but if it trips again straight away the unit needs service rather than another reset.

faqs.q: Can a humming disposal be repaired, or does it need replacing?
faqs.a: Most humming disposals are jams and are repaired by clearing the obstruction. If the plate will not free up, the bearings have seized or the overload keeps tripping, the motor is at fault and replacing the unit is normally cheaper than repairing it.

faqs.q: What should never go down a garbage disposal?
faqs.a: Grease and cooking oil, coffee grounds, eggshells in quantity, fibrous scraps like celery and corn husks, pasta and rice that swell, plus bones and fruit pits. Always run cold water before, during and for a few seconds after grinding.

samsung-ice-maker-freezing-up.title: Samsung Ice Maker Freezing Up? Why It Keeps Happening
samsung-ice-maker-freezing-up.seo_title: Samsung Ice Maker Freezing Up? Why and Fixes
samsung-ice-maker-freezing-up.meta_description: Samsung French-door ice maker frosting over and jamming? The cause is warm air reaching the ice box. Why it recurs and what actually stops it happening.
samsung-ice-maker-freezing-up.excerpt: Clearing the ice out of a Samsung ice maker buys a few weeks. Fixing why warm air reaches the compartment is what stops it coming back.

faqs.q: Why does my Samsung ice maker keep freezing up?
faqs.a: Because warm, humid air is reaching a compartment designed to stay sealed and cold. A hardened or torn gasket around the ice box, a blocked or leaking cold-air duct, or a fill valve that drips between cycles are the usual causes. Clearing the ice without fixing one of those means it returns within weeks.

faqs.q: Can I just melt the ice myself?
faqs.a: You can, carefully: unplug the refrigerator and use a hair dryer on a low setting at a distance, or run the forced defrost routine if your model has one. Never chip at the ice with a metal tool — the mold, auger and refrigerant lines puncture easily.

faqs.q: Why does the ice maker refreeze a few weeks after I clear it?
faqs.a: Because the underlying cause was never addressed. Melting the ice removes the symptom; a leaking seal, a faulty duct or a dripping fill valve keeps putting moisture back into the compartment, and it refreezes on the same schedule.

faqs.q: Is a Samsung ice maker worth repairing?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Gaskets, ducts, fill valves and even the complete ice maker assembly are contained parts, and the repair is far less than replacing a French-door refrigerator. You get a free estimate before any work, so you can compare.

faqs.q: Do you repair Samsung refrigerators in Houston?
faqs.a: Yes. Samsung refrigerators are among the appliances we service most, including French-door, side-by-side and four-door Flex models, with same-day visits across Houston and nearby cities.

bosch-dishwasher-not-drying.title: Bosch Dishwasher Not Drying? How Condensation Drying Works
bosch-dishwasher-not-drying.seo_title: Bosch Dishwasher Not Drying Dishes? Fixes
bosch-dishwasher-not-drying.meta_description: Bosch dishwashers dry by condensation, not a heating element. Why dishes come out wet, what rinse aid actually does and when it is a real fault.
bosch-dishwasher-not-drying.excerpt: Bosch dishwashers have no drying element, so wet dishes usually mean the rinse temperature, the rinse aid or the vent flap — not a broken machine.

faqs.q: Why does my Bosch dishwasher not dry the dishes?
faqs.a: Most Bosch dishwashers dry by condensation rather than with a heating element: the hot final rinse warms the dishes and the moisture condenses on the cooler stainless tub and drains away. Without rinse aid, with a cool final rinse or with a stuck vent flap, that process does not work and dishes stay wet.

faqs.q: Do Bosch dishwashers need rinse aid?
faqs.a: Yes, far more than brands that dry with a heating element. Rinse aid makes water sheet off the dishes instead of beading, which is what condensation drying depends on. Running one without rinse aid will leave dishes wet and spotted even when nothing is broken.

faqs.q: Why are my plastic containers still wet but the glasses are dry?
faqs.a: Because condensation drying relies on dishes holding heat from the final rinse. Glass and ceramic retain that heat; plastic does not, so plastics stay damp. That is normal behaviour for this design rather than a fault.

faqs.q: Is poor drying ever a real fault on a Bosch dishwasher?
faqs.a: Yes. A stuck or failed vent flap, a failed heating circuit or a control fault all stop the drying process properly. The giveaway is glass and ceramic coming out wet, not just plastics, and often poorer cleaning at the same time.

faqs.q: Do you repair Bosch dishwashers in Houston?
faqs.a: Yes. Bosch dishwashers are one of the appliances we repair most often, including the 300, 500, 800 and Benchmark series, with same-day service across Houston and nearby cities and a free estimate before any work.
